content.text: The recently concluded India AI Impact Summit 2026 showcased how India envisions the next phase of artificial intelligence (AI): ambitious in scope, practical in design, and focused on real-world deployment. Alongside agenda-setting conversations around trust, security, and scalable adoption of population-scale AI, the event came alive through live demonstrations and imaginative displays. Reporting for The Economic Times, Dhruv Mohan visited several display booths at the event, where exhibitors showcased their working systems, products, and prototypes. His coverage captured the wave of innovations, offering a ground-level view of how enterprises are translating AI aspirations into deployable, real-world solutions.At HCLTech’s booth, Mohan shifted focus to HCLSoftware, the company’s enterprise software division, which was showcasing its approach to “digital sovereignty”. Here, sovereignty was framed not as a catchphrase but as an engineering requirement: the ability to run models locally, keep sensitive information on-premises or in a private cloud, and still deliver the convenience and responsiveness people now expect from AI-first products.Domino Workspace: one suite, local AI, and collaboration that stays in-houseThe first demo featured HCL Domino, introduced by Rishab Sharma, who framed the product in the context of current market shifts and the pivot from governments and large enterprises to maintain both data and AI sovereignty.“We actually have a solution for the same. It’s called Domino Workspace,” Sharma said, positioning it as “sovereign AI and collaboration.”On screen, Domino Workspace appeared as an all-in-one work environment, bringing together a homepage, mail, calendar, meetings, chat, file sharing, and document creation and collaboration, along with Low Code No Code Application Development capability. The AI positioning was not about a single, monolithic model, but about a “bring your own model” approach around flexibility and choice called Domino IQ.“We also have a chatbot that uses our Domino IQ powers, which will reference your data internally so that you can get responses that are inferred by your local LLM engine,” Sharma explains.A second layer of the demo focused on a policy hub, which was powered by Domino IQ and using HR Policies Data as a reference so that it can respond to HR questions and function like an internal assistant. It served as a straightforward example, but summarised the core pitch: a workplace suite gains value when it can speak the company’s internal language, and it becomes safer when it learns from enterprise knowledge without exporting that knowledge outside the organisation.Mohan distilled the message into a clear takeaway: “So, you have got everything under one roof, a one-stop shop for Sovereign Collaboration and AI.” BigFix: From secure, resilient operations to agent-driven automation with orchestrationFrom collaboration to operations, Mohan then moved to HCL BigFix, introduced by Bharat Bhargava, who presented it as a broad portfolio aimed at secure, resilient operations across data centers, hybrid cloud, and digital workplace environments.The list of capabilities was intentionally exhaustive: observability, intelligent event management, service management, intelligent automation, endpoint management, patching, security, and compliance. These are the kinds of functions that rarely attract attention until something breaks.The centrepiece of the demo was what Bharat described as an “Agentic AI-driven Conversational Automation Platform”, described as BigFix AEX. The emphasis was less on simply “chatting with IT,” but more on building task-specific agents that could execute work on behalf of users. “Customers can create AI agents… very, very task-specific,” Bharat said, noting that teams could also “enable multi-agent orchestration workflows.”To illustrate this, he walked through an employee onboarding scenario, in which a new hire completed the entire process through a conversation interface rather than switching between multiple tools. The primary onboarding agent connected with sub-agents to facilitate actions such as meeting room booking, laptop allocation, and other day-one tasks. Each agent had its own “context and memory,” tied to internal repositories or training datasets, and each agent could be paired with a model chosen by the customer.The scenario Bharat described, from waiting for laptops to raising tickets and following up on mandatory training, is commonplace in most corporate settings. “From an employee, the experience will be purely conversational,” he said, adding that the platform “will try and raise a request on my behalf so that I don’t really have to raise a ticket.”Unica+: Marketing gets a co-pilot, but with approvals punched inThe next demo featured HCL Unica+, a MarTech platform with “AI agent tech” so marketers can do their jobs “even better”, explained Karunesh Abrol. The demo used a marketer persona, Ananya, who opened a dashboard and spotted a problem with email performance for credit card activations. The platform introduced Max AI, positioned as a “co-pilot for marketing.”Ananya asked Max AI what’s wrong; it explains the issue and proposes a fix. Then it nudged her: Do you want to create a new campaign? When she agreed, a marketing-specific agent guided her through steps aimed at improving ROI.“This is all human in the loop, without the approval of a marketer, nothing moves,” Karnesh explains. Each step required sign-off, and the AI also offered its reasoning, explaining why it made particular recommendations. “The models are local. So your data remains your data,” Karnesh said, adding that the sovereignty theme is “really achieved” in this setup.Mohan reflected the underlying selling point that many off-the-shelf tools don’t understand the internal texture of an organisation, but systems trained and tuned inside the enterprise can.“It knows your organisation really well,” he says.Actian Data Intelligence Platform: Put governance and context between AI and enterprise dataThe final demo shifted to a quieter but critical layer of data correctness, access control, and traceability. Cuan DeVries introduced the Actian Data Intelligence Platform, calling it a “contextual layer” that ensures data used by AI is accurate, access is appropriate, and people can understand where the data came from and why it exists.“When you’ve got AI models trying to get that data, it knows exactly what the data is, where it’s coming from, and why it’s actually there,” he said.The screen displayed a data observability system monitoring pipelines over the last 30 days, flagging anomalies and automatically creating tickets (via Jira or other service tools), so issues get proactively resolved instead of overlooked. Cuan highlighted one specific risk: data drift, the gradual shift in patterns that’s easy for teams to miss until it starts affecting results. “Drift is something that happens really slowly and is difficult for people to identify and pick up,” he said. The platform’s internal model predicts expected ranges based on historical data and when the latest scan falls outside that range, the system flags it and triggers action. He expanded to a broader data foundation, which includes a catalogue, lineage, and marketplace that lets teams track inputs into reports like Power BI. Through this example, he addressed a fear that sits behind many AI boardroom conversations: if an AI output is wrong, can we trace the cause fast enough to prevent damage? “If something’s happened in AI, something’s hallucinated, we can track exactly where that’s come from,” Cuan said, noting that “we can fix it immediately before it creates a catastrophic effect.”Throughout the demonstrations, the message that stood out was that AI should be embedded into the suites already used by people and protected through security layersBy the end of the walkthrough, it was clear how Actian empowers data teams and AI agents to discover, trust, and activate data at scale. By creating a solid data foundation, enterprises can quickly make informed decisions while maintaining governance and compliance across the organisation.Disclaimer: This article is generated and published by ET Spotlight team.
